text: Writing clean code is important for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps other developers work with it. Good naming conventions, such as using clear and meaningful names for variables and functions, make code much easier to follow. Functions should be small and do one specific job, so they are simple to test and reuse. When code is clean and well organised, it becomes easier to maintain over time. This means fixing bugs and adding new features takes less effort. In short, writing clean code saves time and reduces problems for the whole team.
